title: Never been more horrified- details below!!
text:
Never been more horrified- details below!!. IM SO CONFUSED- trying for the first time… In order to make solid suction connection- I had to place nozzle so far into the toilet drain.. which was horrifying in itself, pushing through all the items clogging the toilet to begin with- BUT, after nozzle finally sealed opening- Blue portion of the plunger was 90% into the drain hole.. OK fine. However, once unclogged and I backed plunger out.. I was horrified!! The entire plunger was full of toilet debris and of the worst kind!! How in the world could anyone think this was a good idea…??!!

If you think of this logically it’s like plowing into and through what you don’t want to plow through.. Then, having 20-30oz of whatever is clogging the toilet now, all scooped up into the blue elongated portion of plunger. So, when removing plunger itself- all of that “yuck” is inside the elongated hose… And it comes out and dumps back into the toilet?!! OMG- I must have faith that something didn’t work as expected because, if this is accurate- it should never be used again. Not to mention I can’t even fathom what the interior of the blue nozzle is covered in and no, I did not want to wash it and find out!!
What makes no sense… I’ve used a standard size plunger and it worked perfectly on those unpleasant situations.. And this is on a standard size toilet mind you. So, how anyone could possibly appreciate what has to take place in order to get suction with this plunger- seems a bit mine boggling.

I’m not going to experience this again and therefore, I am going to discard this and go back to the tried and true original style and be happy about it. To each his own… Just know, this is One of those things I’d like to not have to talk about again!
Sorry so Crass- hoping this info can help you avoid a yucky experience!!
